summary: universities.data_status does not reliably reflect the image-pipeline's needs_review gate; the dedicated primary_image_status/notes columns described in the mission brief do not exist in this DB at all.
details: Ran a read-only cross-check of all 42 assigned rn's against Supabase project qtcvcflzxbuagvvwahhu. Two findings: (1) `information_schema.columns` has no column matching '%image%' anywhere in the public schema, and no table matching '%media%'/'%asset%'/'%photo%'/'%storage%' - so the `primary_image_status` / `notes` fields the mission brief describes on `universities` are not persisted anywhere I could find; my only source for the per-university rejection reason was the input JSON file itself, not the live DB. (2) Of the 42 assigned universities, 11 currently show `universities.data_status = 'fresh'` rather than 'needs_review' (rn 760 Melbourne, 807 UC Irvine, 846 Caltech, 872 Stockholm, 927 Lancaster, 929 Strathclyde, 952 Griffith, 968 Fudan, 974 ULB, 982 Lund, 996 UAB), including 2 (807 UC Irvine, and several others) that already have a non-null `logo_url`. This strongly suggests `data_status` is a general data-freshness flag shared with other refresh jobs (e.g. the Phase-30 'university information freshness' job) - when that job re-verifies unrelated fields (admissions, statistics) it appears to overwrite the same enum value that the image pipeline had set to 'needs_review', silently erasing the image-specific signal even though the photo issue was never actually resolved. Net effect: `data_status` cannot currently be trusted as an indicator of whether a university's photo has been fixed - both false 'fresh' (photo still broken) and stale 'needs_review' (photo already fine) are possible.
recommendation: Do not resolve in this task (read-only, out of scope). Flagging for whoever owns lib/acquisition/image-validation.ts and the universities schema: consider a dedicated primary_image_status column (or a jsonb sub-object) separate from the general data_status freshness flag, so the two review workflows stop clobbering each other.
